prompt: The Zappone family has a rectangular table that seats eight people: three people on each of the longer sides and one person on each of the shorter sides. Eight people will sit down to Thanksgiving dinner. Grady, who is 3 years old and can't read yet, is asked to place a pre-printed name card at each table setting to indicate where everyone should sit. What is the probability that Uncle Rob's name card will be placed at a table setting along one of the two shorter sides of the table? Express your answer as a common fraction.

solutions.title: Favorable seats over all seats
solutions.body:
Since Grady can't read, Uncle Rob's card is equally likely to land at any of the 8 settings. Two of them are on the short sides, so the probability is $\frac{2}{8} = \frac14$.

**Answer: $\frac14$**

solutions.title: Complement
solutions.body:
The chance his card is on a long side is $\frac{6}{8} = \frac34$, so the chance it is on a short side is $1 - \frac34 = \frac14$.

**Answer: $\frac14$**

prompt: For Thanksgiving dinner, Mrs. Zappone is preparing a huge turkey, as well as potatoes, carrots, green beans, cranberry salad and dinner rolls. Grandpa Curt takes a little bit of everything, while Grady sticks to turkey and dinner rolls. How many distinct combinations of food items are possible at the Zappone family feast, assuming everyone takes some turkey?

solutions.title: Yes/no for each side dish
solutions.body:
Turkey is always taken. Each of the 5 side dishes is either taken or not, so there are $2^5 = 32$ combinations (including turkey alone).

**Answer: 32**

prompt: Mrs. Zappone baked a round apple pie. Eight equal slices (sectors) of the pie are cut and one piece is distributed to each person at dinner. After this is done, there is exactly $\frac13$ of the pie left. How many degrees are in the central angle of each person's slice of pie?

solutions.title: Angle of the eaten part
solutions.body:
The 8 slices make up $1 - \frac13 = \frac23$ of the pie, which is $\frac23 \times 360° = 240°$. Each slice: $240° \div 8 = 30°$.

**Answer: 30 degrees**

solutions.title: Fraction per slice
solutions.body:
Each slice is $\frac23 \div 8 = \frac{1}{12}$ of the pie, and $\frac{1}{12}$ of $360°$ is $30°$.

**Answer: 30 degrees**
